default: The ruins come on gradually, and then all at once.

First there are stones lying at odd angles in the forest floor, too regular to be natural and too broken to be anything else. You step over them without thinking. Then there are more of them, and then a wall, or a couple of yards of one, standing on its own and ending in nothing. Then there is an archway, with no gate in it and no building on either side, framing a square of grey sky.
Then the ground changes. Under a thin skin of soil there is something harder, a worked surface, the remains of a road or a floor where people once walked about their business.
You are in the ruins.

default.text: Maret stops at the first broken arch. "Three paths go through here," she says. "I found two of them. I never found where the third begins."

default: The silence here is not the silence of the forest. It is heavier, the sort that has built up over centuries rather than hours.
text.commander:
You go through the outskirts as you would clear any position, except that this one has no edges you can find and no enemy you can name.

The ruins are big, bigger than the way in had led you to expect. What you can see above ground is only the top of them. Where the weather has worn the edges away you can see that the building goes down, and a long way down.
text.arcane:
The ruins are thick with the residue of old workings, things done here over centuries. It is not the curse; it is older than that. This was a busy place once, lived in by people who understood the hidden workings of the world far better than your own tradition has managed to relearn.

You would like to spend a year here. You haven't a year. You take notes and keep moving.
text.ranger:
You look the outskirts over as you would any new ground, for paths, for signs of anyone passing lately, and for places where the ground is less dead than elsewhere.

There are paths. Nobody laid them; they have been worn by use. Something or somebody has been going through these ruins regularly. And the paths all run together, towards the middle.
text.cipher:
The place has a plan to it. You spend the first twenty minutes working it out in your head: which parts you can get into and which are blocked, where the open ground is, and where the walls narrow it down.

Somebody has done the same before you. You can see the small signs of it, a stone moved here and a gap cleared there. People have been finding their way through these ruins, lately and often.

choices.text: Follow the worn paths and see where they go.

bonus.label: Maret found two of the paths

success.text:
Once you know what to look for, the paths are clearer than you expected. There are three of them through the outskirts, and each keeps clear of certain places where the ground is wrong in a way you are learning to recognise. The curse lies thicker there.

Somebody worked out these paths by trial and error, and probably painful error.

Where all three paths meet there is a cairn. It is new, built within the last week. On the top of it lies a scrap of cloth with a stone on it to hold it down, and you know the cloth.

success_at_cost.text:
You find the paths, but it costs you something. You spend half an hour in the thicker parts before you hit on the safe ways through, and all that time the curse presses harder on you than it ever has.

At least you know now what it is like when it is strong. You keep moving.

failure.text:
You go through the outskirts without making out the paths, and you pay for it. You spend twenty minutes in places where the curse lies thick, and with every step the world becomes a little less interesting.

In the end you find the cairn by accident.

choices.text: Stop and look the ruins over carefully before you go further.

success.text:
You find three things in your first careful look.

The first is that the ruins are not haphazard. What you can see is laid out round a centre, like the spokes of a wheel, and everything faces towards a point that is now underground or fallen in. This was a city built round a middle, and the middle mattered.

The second is that the stone is wrong. It hums, very faintly, just below hearing. The curse is using the stone to travel through.

The third is that somebody has been here within the last week. They left traces that are easy to miss and hard to explain away once you have seen them.

success_at_cost.text: You make out the plan of the place, built round a centre and facing it. But you don't see the signs of anybody passing until you are very nearly standing on the cairn.

failure.text: The ruins tell you how big they are and nothing more useful. You can see that they are large and old and face towards something, but that is all. You move on.

default: The cairn stands where three paths through the outskirts meet, in a spot where the curse lies a little thinner than round about. It may be chance, or it may not.
There is a piece of cloth on top of it, held down by a flat stone. You know the cloth before you pick it up. You would know it anywhere.

default.text: "That is their hand," Maret says. She doesn't touch the stone.

default: Under the cloth, scratched into the flat stone in small careful letters, there is a message.
*I am below. Take the south passage. Do not touch the carved walls. Wait at the gate.*
The scratches are fresh. Whoever wrote this knew you were already over the line.

There is no name and no date. But it is their writing, and the instruction is plain enough. You look about for the south passage and find it, a gap between two standing walls that does not look like a gap at all until you come at it from the right angle.
text.commander:
It reads like an order: where to meet, which way to go, what not to do, and where to wait. They expected you, or somebody, and they made ready.

Fourteen months in the ruins, and they can still plan ahead. That is worth knowing.
text.arcane:
The message is in plain words, but the stone is no ordinary stone. It is one of the humming stones from the ruins, chosen on purpose, because it will keep the writing longer than paper would. They knew that.

So they have been learning how this place works, for fourteen months. Somebody has been at work here, and they have got a good deal further than you.
text.ranger:
You look at the ground round the cairn. The path to the south passage is more worn than the others; it is the one most used. They come back here often, and they have been keeping the cairn up.

They are not lost. They are living here.
text.cipher:
The message is brisk, with no feeling in it and no explanation and no doubt. Either they knew you would come, which means they trusted you a great deal, and you can't decide whether that is touching or calculating, or else they left it for anybody capable who got this far.

You go to the south passage.

choices.text: Do as it says: the south passage, keep off the walls, and wait at the gate.

default.text:
You go to the south passage. Keeping off the carved walls takes some care, for the passage is narrow and the carving runs further than you first thought, right down to the floor. You pick your way through and come out into a wider space.

The gate is ahead of you. It is not a gate any longer; the walls it hung in have mostly fallen. But the frame still stands, two upright stones with another across the top, and in its shadow somebody is sitting, waiting.

choices.text: Go through the south passage fast, before the walls can get into your head.

success.text: You find the gap between the walls and go through it at a run, with your eyes on the ground and your shoulders in. The carved stone goes past on both sides, close enough to feel. You don't look at it. On the far side you stop, and get your breath, and only then turn round.

success_at_cost.text: You go fast, and nearly make it. At the narrowest point your sleeve drags along the wall, and for a moment you can think of nothing but the carvings, line after line of them. Then you are through, and it stops.

failure.text: You misjudge the narrow place. Your shoulder hits the wall, and then your hand, flat on the carving. It is like putting your hand into cold water and finding there is no bottom. You don't know how long you stand there. When you come out at the other side your hand is still cold.

choices.text: Look at the carved walls before you go on. They may tell you something.

success.text:
You look without touching. The carvings are in a script you cannot read, but there are pictures among the writing, and those you can follow. They tell a story in order: something shut in, something breaking, something spreading. And at the end, scratched in fresh with a different tool and by a different hand, something stopped.

The last picture was added lately, by somebody who understood the story and wanted to show that the last part could still be done.

success_at_cost.text:
While you are studying the carvings you touch the wall by accident. It is only the plain stone beside them, but the effect is immediate and unpleasant. The narrowing comes over you, harder than you have ever felt it, for four or five seconds.

You understand now why the message told you not to touch them. You go on more carefully.

failure.text: You can make nothing of the carvings at all. You do as the message said, keep clear of them, and go on.

text.default:
The figure at the gate is not [missing person].

You know it at once; the height is wrong, and so is the way they sit. They are sitting with their back against the right-hand stone of the gate, with their knees drawn up and their face turned a little away from you.

They are wearing Harrow clothes, the grey wool the village used for outdoor work. The clothes are whole. The person inside them is not.

They are alive; you can see them breathing. But when you come near they don't answer. They don't turn at your footsteps, or at your voice when you try it, or at anything at all. Their eyes are open and fixed on something that is not here.

The Watcher. The camp has a name for this. You heard it at the fire and did not ask what it meant, and now you know.
text.commander:
You look the Watcher over quickly. Alive, and not answering, and no danger to you. The body is easy, not braced. They are not asleep. Their eyes are open and following something, only not anything you can see.

This is the furthest you have seen the curse go in a person who can still walk. Whatever they were, they are now mostly a signal.
text.arcane:
You have never come across residue like the Watcher's. It isn't the curse as you have known it. They have been in the ruins so long that you can no longer tell where the curse stops and they begin. They are not suffering from the curse. In some sense they have become part of it.

That ought to disturb you more than it does. It does not disturb you nearly enough, and that disturbs you rather more.
text.ranger:
The Watcher doesn't take any notice of you, as a person would, or even as a badly afflicted person would. They are like a marker set at the edge of a territory. They are not here by chance. They have been put here.

Something put them here, and is using them as you would use a cairn.
text.cipher:
The Watcher is telling you something. Somebody put them here, at the gate, at the very place the message on the cairn sent you to. Whether that somebody was [missing person], or the ruins themselves, or something else altogether, is the question.

You watch the Watcher, and wait.

choices.text: Try to reach the Watcher. They were a person once.

success.text:
You crouch in front of them and speak. You don't know their name, so you just talk, calmly and plainly, as you would to somebody coming up out of very deep water.

Something in their eyes moves, very slightly, as though something were coming back from a long way off.

They say one word. "[player]."

Then they have gone again, back to wherever they were. But nobody here told the Watcher that name today. Somebody who has been in here a very long time told the Watcher your name, and the Watcher has said it.

success_at_cost.text: You try, and for a moment something moves in them. They seem to turn towards you a little, and to know you are there, and it costs you something to look at. Then it passes. They didn't speak, but they saw you. Or something behind them did.

failure.text: Nothing. The Watcher is not there to be spoken to. You stand up and look at the gate. The message said to wait at the gate, so you wait.

choices.text: Reach for them the way the curse does.

success.text:
You stop trying to make them hear you. You let yourself go still, as they are still, and stop wanting anything of them.

Something in their eyes moves, very slightly, as though something were coming back from a long way off.

They say one word. "[player]."

Then they have gone again, back to wherever they were. But nobody here told the Watcher that name today. Somebody who has been in here a very long time told the Watcher your name, and the Watcher has said it.

success_at_cost.text:
You stop trying to make them hear you. You let yourself go still, as they are still, and stop wanting anything of them.

For a moment something moves in them. They seem to know you are there, and it costs you something to look at. Then it passes. They didn't speak, but they saw you. Or something behind them did.

failure.text: You let yourself go still, and go on going. The note is very loud here. When you find your way back you are sitting against the other stone with your knees drawn up, and the light has moved.

choices.text: Set the bone figure on the ground in front of them.
choices.locked_hint: Needs the bone figure from Harrow

default.text:
You crouch down, set the figure on the stone in front of their boots, and step back.

Nothing happens. Then, slowly, one hand comes down off their knee and finds it, as a hand finds a cup in the dark. They hold it. They don't look at it. Their thumb moves over the face that isn't there.

choices.text: Do as the message says, and wait at the gate.

default.text:
You settle yourself near the gate and wait. The Watcher doesn't look at you. The ruins are quiet in their own way, and the time goes by without anything to mark it, as it has since you came into the forest.

Then, from somewhere deeper in, there are footsteps.

default: There are footsteps, from deeper in the ruins, beyond the gate.

It is a step you know. You have not heard it for more than a year, but before that you heard it so often that you know it as you know anything you have heard a thousand times, without having to think.

default.text: Maret steps back.

choices.text: Go on.

default: They come through the gate.

They have changed. You see it at once, and make yourself take it in before you let yourself feel anything. They are thinner; they have been living on what the forest gives. And their eyes are not the empty eyes of the afflicted. If anything they are the opposite. They seem to see more than you do, and to have done so for a long time.

default.text: Then they push their hair back with the heel of their hand, as they did at twelve when they were about to dare you to something, and they have not changed at all.
Then they tilt their head, very slightly, to the left, as they used to when you said something they had not expected. You thought you had forgotten that.
They stand with their weight on one foot and their arms folded, as your mother used to stand in the kitchen doorway. They always hated it when you told them so.
They stop with their hands behind their back and look you up and down, as they did at the start of every lesson, before they said anything at all.
They rub a thumb across their knuckles, first one hand and then the other, as they did when they waited up for you. You were always late.
They put a hand on the gatepost as they come through, lightly, as if the stone might want steadying. You knew they would do that, though you could not say how.

default: They see you, and stop.
Neither of you moves.
text.commander:
You have had reunions before, with people you thought were dead and people you went back for. You know how this goes. Everything stops, and then the world has to rearrange itself round something new.

They are alive, and here, and changed.

You do what you always do at such moments. You move first, and cross the distance between you.
text.arcane:
It takes you less than a second to read them, and it will take you the rest of the day to understand what you have read.

The curse is in them, though not deeply. There is no emptiness in them, and nothing has been taken away. It has become part of them in a way you have never seen before. They have not caught the curse. They have been learning it, as one learns a language, slowly, until it is not foreign any more.

You don't know whether that is extraordinary or disastrous. Very possibly it is both.
text.ranger:
You look them over as you would ground that something has happened to, for what has changed, what has held, and what the change has cost.

They held. That is what you see first. Fourteen months in the ruins, and they held. Whatever makes them themselves is still there and still plain to see. They have changed round the edges, and grown harder in the middle.

They are looking at you in exactly the same way.
text.cipher:
You read them, and find something you did not expect. They are reading you. They are looking at you as you look at people, weighing what they see against what they expected to see.

Fourteen months in the ruins have taught them something. You are not sure you want them to have learned it, and you are not sure it is something you can ask them to give back.

choices.text: Cross the distance and go to them.

default.text:
You cross the distance.

It is not a reunion as reunions are in stories. It is quieter than that, and more careful. You are two people who have been carrying something for a long time, working out between you how to put it down without breaking it.

"[missing person]," you say.

"[player]," they say.

The rest can wait.

choices.text: Stay where you are. Let them come to you.

text: You stay where you are, and they understand. You are here, you will wait, and they may take as long as they need.
They take a breath. Then they cross the distance.

They stop a foot away from you. They are close enough for you to see exactly how the fourteen months have changed them, and to see, under the changes, the person you have carried about with you since you got on the barge at Crestfall.
They are not altogether glad. "I told you not to."

default: You sit down together at the foot of the gate stones, near the Watcher, though that does not seem to trouble them. They have been near the Watcher for months.

default.text:
They look past you. "Maret."

"I should have come sooner," Maret says. She says nothing else, not yet.

default: They talk, and at first you only listen.

They came in fourteen months ago looking for the source of the curse, along the same trail Maret gave them. They got to the marker line and went past it. They found the inner approach and followed it down, and they found the source chamber. The old sealing mechanism is there, broken, and the curse is coming out of it through the stone and the soil and the water of Ashenveld.
And they found the sealing ritual, the whole of the original text, carved on the walls of the chamber. They have spent fourteen months learning to read it.

choices.text: Go on.

text.default:
"I can seal it," they say. "I know how. But the ritual takes two people, and I have been on my own."

They look at you. They need not say anything more. It has been plain since the message on the cairn and the cloth at the camp, and very likely since the letter that brought you here.
text.commander:
"You planned this," you say. You say it without anger, as a plain fact.

"I hoped," they say, and you hear the difference. "I hoped you would come, and I hoped you would be willing. I left marks at every place where I thought they would tell you what you were walking into, without telling you what I needed from you."

They pause. "I did not want to ask you before you knew what you would be agreeing to."

That is either the most considerate thing anybody has ever done for you, or a kind of managing so delicate that you would never notice it. Very possibly it is both.
text.arcane:
The part of you that has been studying such things for eleven years takes it all in at once. The original sealing ritual, needing two people, and fourteen months spent learning it alone.

"What does the ritual ask of the second person?" you ask.

The pause before they answer tells you more than anything they say.
text.ranger:
"You've been in there," you say. You mean the source chamber. "Past the marker line, right in the middle of it."

"Yes."

"For fourteen months."

"Yes."

You look at them, at the whole of them and not just their face. You have never before seen what fourteen months in the source chamber does to a person the curse has not taken. You are still making up your mind what you are seeing.
text.cipher:
"The letter," you say. "The marks at the camp. The cairn. You planned all of it."

"Yes," they say. They don't apologise. They made a choice and they will stand by it.

"You needed me to come here," you say. "Not because you missed me. Because you needed a second person for the ritual."

They are silent, and the silence is an answer. Then they say, "I missed you as well." They say it as though it mattered very much that you should believe it.

choices.text: "What does the ritual ask of me?"

default.text:
They tell you.

The ritual needs two people who are, and here the text uses a word they have spent months trying to translate, and the nearest they can come is bonded. They don't mean married or sworn. They mean two people whose lives have shaped each other, who carry each other about, so that to part one from the other would change what both of them are made of.

The ritual will work with any two such people.

They chose you.

"And the risk?" you ask.

They pause again. "There is a risk for both of us. I do not know how much. The text is honest about it; the people who wrote it were honest." They look at you. "I did not bring you here to kill you. But I cannot promise you will come out of it as you went in."

choices.text: "Before anything else, are you all right?"

text: The question takes them by surprise. They had got ready for practical questions, and you have asked them a human one.

"I am..." They stop, and begin again. "I am different. I do not know whether different is the same as all right. I have been inside this place for fourteen months, and it has changed how I see things." They pause. "It is not like the affliction, or the dimming. I have been looking at a thing for so long that I understand the shape of it now. And once you understand the shape of something, you cannot stop understanding it."

text.text: Then, quieter: "You still stand like you're about to run."
Then, before they can stop it: "You cut your hair."
Then: "You look like her. Did anyone tell you? You look like her now."
Then: "You came through the outskirts on your own. I saw your marks. You did it properly."
Then, as if it were the obvious thing to ask: "Have you been eating?"
Then, very quietly: "I thought about what I would say if you came. I did not think of anything."

text: They look at you steadily. "I am glad you came. That is true, ritual or no ritual."

choices.text: "You told me to go home. Then you gave the Watcher my name."

text: "I meant it," they say. "Go home. I meant it when I wrote it." They look at the gate stones and not at you. "Then I read the chamber wall properly. It needs two. And there was only ever one name I could give it."
"I wanted you safe, and I needed you here. I have not found a way to make those the same thing."
Then they tell you what the ritual needs.

It needs two people who are, and here the text uses a word they have spent months trying to translate, and the nearest they can come is bonded. They don't mean married or sworn. They mean two people whose lives have shaped each other, who carry each other about, so that to part one from the other would change what both of them are made of.
The ritual will work with any two such people.

choices.text: Show them the cloth.

default.text:
You take out the cloth and put it in their hands. They read their own writing twice.

"I wrote that in the dark," they say. "I could not see if the ink was taking." They fold it once and give it back. "Keep it. You came anyway."

choices.locked_hint: Needs the cloth from the campsite

text.default:
They tell you all they know, in the order they found it out.

The ruins are what is left of a city built to hold in the power that is now leaking out as the curse. The builders knew the power was there. They did not make it. They found it in the ground, already ancient, and built their city round the mechanism that held it, and kept it in order for generations. Then something happened to them, and their records stop.

Whatever stopped them is not in the ruins. But the mechanism is still there. It is broken, but it can be mended, and the ritual for mending it is cut into the walls of the chamber.

choices.text: Go on.

default: "How badly broken?" you ask.
"Badly enough," they say. "The seal has been failing for about twenty years. Three years ago it failed altogether. That is when the curse began to spread."

default.text: Twenty years of slow failure. Edric said a scholar was coming from the capital. You wonder how old she is.
default.else: Twenty years of slow failure. You wonder who was in here twenty years ago, and what they were doing.

text.commander:
"The Covenant knows this," you say.

"Some of it," they say. "The Covenant has texts about the first sealing. They know the ritual exists, and I think they have part of it. But the whole text, the version that works, is on the walls of the chamber. I have copied it."

They bring out a journal, battered and closely written: fourteen months of work.

"Anyone who got hold of that," you say, "could do the ritual."

"Yes," they say. "That is why I need to do it before anyone else does."
text.arcane:
You take it in as hungrily as you take in anything that matters, and you begin at once to ask what follows from it.

"The power the city was holding in," you say. "What is it?"

They are quiet for a moment. "The nearest I can come," they say, "is that it is the world's first power to change. It is not evil, and it is not good. It is everything the world might become if nothing held it as it is." They pause. "Let loose, it does not destroy things. It changes them, without stopping, into more and more purely what they are. The curse is what that looks like at the edges. People become so entirely themselves that the part of them that cares about anything outside wears away."

You sit and think about that. It changes everything you thought you knew about the curse.
text.ranger:
"The animals," you say. "The ones that move wrong. The deer."

"Yes," they say. "It goes faster in them than in people. They have less of what it wears away. They become nothing but instinct, nothing but movement. The deer you saw is only the part of a deer that runs and feeds, and there is nothing else left."

You look at the Watcher. "And people?"

"People become nothing but presence. They attend, without attending to anything. They are, without wanting." They follow your eyes. "He is not suffering. I want you to know that. He is not in there going without. He is simply there, entirely."
text.cipher:
You take it in as you would any report, and you see at once what it means.

A ritual exists that works. [missing person] has a copy, and the Covenant has part of one. The Compact does not know it exists, and will want it when it finds out. And Pol, at the Rootless camp, left the Covenant after reading something in its archives.

"Pol," you say.

They look at you. "You know Pol."

"She's at the Rootless camp. She left the Covenant fifteen years ago."

Their face changes. "Then she read the whole text," they say. "That is the only reason anybody leaves the Covenant."

choices.text: "How long have we got before the curse reaches Crestfall?"

default.text:
"Weeks," they say. "Perhaps less. It has been getting faster. Every time the mechanism wears a little more, the curse spreads more quickly." They look at you steadily. "We should do the ritual soon. Not today. You have only just come, and you need to understand the chamber before you go into it. But not weeks from now, either."

They get up. "I will show you the inner approach, and the chamber. I will show you what the ritual needs and what it risks. And then you can decide."

choices.text: Tell them what has been happening in Crestfall: the Compact, the Covenant, all of it.

default.text:
You tell them all of it: Maret, the Compact, Cael and Edric, and the two names you heard before you left. A Commander Vorne is expected, and a scholar called Seriva.

At Seriva's name they go quite still.

"Seriva," they say. "She was here twenty years ago. I found her visit in the chamber records. The ruins keep a kind of record of who has been inside them." They speak carefully. "She was here when the mechanism began to fail. The records say she was in the chamber."

Neither of you says anything for a moment.

"She caused this," you say.

"I do not know that," they say. "But I think she knows what caused it. And I think she has spent twenty years trying to put it right in a way that would never require her to admit what she did."

choices.text: Show them the cellar carvings.

default.text:
You open your journal at the page and turn it to the firelight.

They go through it line by line. Then they put a finger on one mark, a line running down between two others, and say, "That is not the passage I use."

"Is it a way in?"

"It is a way down." They look at you. "Somebody from Harrow came this far and drew it on a wall. Tomorrow we find out if he was right."

default: You don't remember how it ended.

default.text:
You wake in a room at the Tallow with your boots still on. The light says it is morning, and the wrong morning, too, for a day has gone. Somebody has left water by the bed and a heel of bread on a plate.

Aldous is in the doorway. "Two of them brought you in," he says. "I didn't ask where from."

You wake under canvas, with the smell of the camp fire and somebody's coat over you. It is morning, and you have lost a day.

Maret is sitting on an upturned crate by the tent flap. "Branch carried you," she says. "Do not thank him. He will not know what to do with it."

You wake on a pallet at the back of the shrine, under the grey banner. It is morning, and a day has gone.

Edric is lighting the candles one at a time. "You were found on the steps," he says, without turning round.

You wake by the fire in the outskirts. The light is the same grey as always, but [missing person] tells you a day has gone.

"You stopped," they say. "In the middle of a sentence. I talked to you until you came back."

default: You sit up. Your hands are steady enough.

choices.text: Get up.

default.text: You get dressed and go back out.
